1001.explicacion: The 1978 Constitution says that Spain's political form is a «monarquía parlamentaria» (parliamentary monarchy). The king is head of State, but political power lies with Parliament and the Government. Spain is neither a republic nor a federal state. Tip: king plus Parliament equals parliamentary monarchy.

1002.explicacion: Spain's fundamental law is the «Constitución» (Constitution), approved in 1978. It is the most important rule: all other laws must respect it. «Ley básica» and «Ordenamiento esencial» are not real names. Tip: the Constitution is the base that «constitutes» the State.

1003.texto: According to the Spanish Constitution, national sovereignty lies with…
opciones: the Congreso de los Diputados (Chamber of Deputies).
1003.explicacion: The Constitution says national sovereignty lies with «el pueblo español» (the Spanish people). All powers of the State come from the people. The Government and Congress have power because citizens vote, but they do not own sovereignty. Tip: in a democracy, power comes from the people.

1004.texto: The Instituto de las Mujeres (Women's Institute) is…
1004.explicacion: The «Instituto de las Mujeres» is «un organismo español» (a Spanish public body) that belongs to the Ministry of Equality. It works for real equality between women and men in Spain. It is not a European Union institution or an NGO, because it is part of the public administration.

1005.texto: When can I carry out procedures on the sede electrónica (official e-government website)?
1005.explicacion: The «sede electrónica» is an administration's official website for procedures. It is open 24 hours a day, every day of the year. So you can do your procedures «en cualquier horario» (at any time), even at night and at weekends. Tip: the internet never closes.

1006.texto: Castilian or Spanish is an official language…
opciones: only where there are no other languages.
1006.explicacion: Castilian or Spanish is the official language of the State and is official «en toda España» (throughout Spain). Some regions also have a second co-official language, such as Catalan, Galician or Basque. Portugal is also on the peninsula, but its official language is Portuguese.

1007.texto: Which of these security forces operates at the level of an autonomous community?
opciones: Policía Foral de Navarra (Navarre regional police).
1007.explicacion: The «Policía Foral de Navarra» is a regional police force that works only in Navarre, an autonomous community. The «Policía local» belongs to each town, and the «Guardia Civil» is a State force that works all over Spain. Tip: «Navarra» is the name of an autonomous community.

1008.texto: Which security force operates throughout Spain?
opciones: The Policía Foral de Navarra (Navarre regional police).
The Cuerpo Nacional de Policía (National Police).
1008.explicacion: The «Cuerpo Nacional de Policía» is a State force that works all over Spain, especially in cities. The «Policía Foral de Navarra» works only in Navarre and the «Mossos d’Esquadra» only in Catalonia. Tip: the word «Nacional» means the whole country.

1009.texto: The Constitution establishes the separation of powers: the executive, the legislative and the…
1009.explicacion: The Constitution separates three powers: the legislative makes laws, the executive governs and the «judicial» applies the laws in the courts. This way no single power controls everything. «Informativo» and «político» are not powers of the State. Tip: laws, Government and judges.

1010.texto: The Spanish flag must be used…
1010.explicacion: The law says the Spanish flag must be displayed «en todos los edificios públicos» (on all public buildings): it flies outside and has a place of honour inside. It is not used only on holidays or only at Government events. Tip: if a building is public, it has a flag.

1011.texto: Who is the head of State in Spain?
opciones: The President of the Government (Prime Minister).
1011.explicacion: In Spain the head of State is «el rey» (the king). He represents the country at home and abroad. The «presidente del Gobierno» leads the Government but is not head of State, and the Minister for the Economy is just one member of the Government. Tip: king for the State, president for the Government.

1012.texto: Healthcare management is the responsibility of…
1012.explicacion: Managing healthcare is the job of «las comunidades autónomas» (the autonomous communities). Each region has its own health service, with its hospitals and health centres. The State sets the basic rules for the whole country. Tip: your health card is issued by your autonomous community.

1013.texto: Who was the first President of the Government (Prime Minister) of Spain in democracy?
1013.explicacion: «Adolfo Suárez» was the first Prime Minister elected in democracy, in the 1977 elections, after Franco's dictatorship. Mariano Rajoy and José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero governed much later, in the 21st century. Tip: Suárez is the president of the «Transición» (transition to democracy).

1014.texto: Which of these bodies is in charge of interpreting the Constitution?
opciones: The Consejo General del Poder Judicial (General Council of the Judiciary).
1014.explicacion: The «Tribunal Constitucional» (Constitutional Court) is the supreme interpreter of the Constitution. It decides whether a law agrees with the Constitution and protects fundamental rights. The «Consejo General del Poder Judicial» governs the judges, and the «Poder Constitucional» does not exist. Tip: Constitution and Constitutional Court go together.

1015.texto: Who moderates the functioning of Spain's institutions?
opciones: The President of the Government (Prime Minister).
The director of the Real Academia Española (Royal Spanish Academy).
1015.explicacion: According to the Constitution, «el rey» (the king) arbitrates and moderates the regular functioning of the institutions. He is a neutral figure, above political parties. The Prime Minister leads policy, and the director of the «Real Academia Española» looks after the language. Tip: the king is the referee.

1016.texto: What is the name of the chamber of territorial representation in Spain?
opciones: Congreso de los Diputados (Chamber of Deputies).
1016.explicacion: The «Senado» (Senate) is the chamber of territorial representation: it represents the provinces, islands and autonomous communities. The «Congreso de los Diputados» is the other chamber of the «Cortes Generales». The «Diputación permanente» only acts when the chambers are not sitting. Tip: Senate means territories.

1017.texto: What do you need to carry out online procedures with the public administration?
1017.explicacion: To carry out online procedures with the administration you must identify yourself and sign digitally. That is what the «firma electrónica» (electronic signature) is for, for example with a digital certificate or the electronic ID card. A paper signature does not work online and a passport is not enough. Tip: electronic procedure, electronic signature.

1018.explicacion: The Spanish Constitution was approved «por referéndum» (by referendum) on 6 December 1978: citizens voted and the majority said yes. That is why Constitution Day is celebrated every 6 December. It was not imposed, and it was not decided by the Constitutional Court, which was created later.

1019.texto: What is the most important law of each autonomous community called?
1019.explicacion: The most important rule of each autonomous community is its «Estatuto de Autonomía» (Statute of Autonomy). It organises the region's institutions and sets out its powers, always respecting the Constitution. «Normativa autonómica» and «Ley de la comunidad» are general expressions, not the name of this law. Tip: autonomous community, Statute of Autonomy.

1020.texto: Public cultural and sports facilities are the responsibility of the…
opciones: Ministry of Education, Vocational Training and Sports.
1020.explicacion: Town councils, the «Ayuntamiento», run many local services, such as the town's public cultural and sports facilities: libraries, sports centres and municipal swimming pools. Ministries work for the whole of Spain and do not manage these neighbourhood places. Tip: if it belongs to the town or city, it is the Ayuntamiento.
1020.nota: For the exam, the answer is «Ayuntamiento», although some public cultural and sports facilities also belong to the autonomous communities or the State.

1021.explicacion: According to the Constitution, «el Gobierno» (the Government) directs domestic and foreign policy, the civil and military administration and the defence of the State. The «Cortes Generales» make laws and oversee the Government, but do not direct the military. Town councils have no military role. Tip: the Government also governs the military.

1022.texto: What do the Balearic Islands have instead of diputaciones (provincial councils)?
1022.explicacion: In the Balearic Islands each main island has its «Consejo insular» (island council), which does work similar to a «diputación». «Cabildos» exist in the Canary Islands, not in the Balearics. «Centros de diputados» do not exist. Tip: Balearics, consejos; Canaries, cabildos.

1023.texto: Which city has the most inhabitants?
1023.explicacion: «Barcelona» has more inhabitants than Seville and Zaragoza: over 1.6 million. It is Spain's second-largest city, after Madrid. Seville and Zaragoza each have fewer than 700,000 people. Tip: Madrid is first and Barcelona is second.

1024.explicacion: The «Cortes Generales» are Spain's Parliament and represent «al pueblo español» (the Spanish people). They are made up of the Chamber of Deputies and the Senate, whose members are elected. They do not represent parties or ministers. Tip: citizens vote, and the Cortes speak for them.

1025.texto: The Congreso de los Diputados (Chamber of Deputies) and the Senado (Senate) make up the … power.
1025.explicacion: The Chamber of Deputies and the Senate form the «Cortes Generales», which hold the «legislativo» (legislative) power: they make and approve laws. Executive power belongs to the Government, and judicial power to judges and courts. Tip: «legislativo» comes from «ley» (law).

1026.texto: How can citizens propose new laws to the Congreso (Congress of Deputies)?
1026.explicacion: Citizens can present an «iniciativa legislativa popular» (popular legislative initiative). They must collect at least 500,000 signatures («firmas»). The king does not propose laws, and creating an association is not enough. Tip: half a million signatures for one law.

1027.texto: How many autonomous communities (comunidades autónomas) are there in Spain?
1027.explicacion: Spain has 17 «comunidades autónomas» (autonomous communities), such as Andalusia, Catalonia and Galicia. There are also two autonomous cities, Ceuta and Melilla, which are not counted among the 17. Tip: 17 communities plus 2 cities.

1028.texto: The colours of the Spanish flag are…
1028.explicacion: The Spanish flag has three horizontal stripes: red, yellow and red. The yellow stripe in the middle is wider and carries the coat of arms. There is no white. In the exam, look for «rojo y amarillo» (red and yellow).

1029.texto: Where is the seat of the Government of Spain?
1029.explicacion: Madrid is the capital of Spain. The Government, the Cortes Generales (Parliament) and the Royal Household are all there. Barcelona and Seville are large cities, but they are not the seat of Government. Tip: capital and Government, both in «Madrid».

1030.texto: The blue flag with 12 yellow stars in a circle is the flag of…
1030.explicacion: The «Unión Europea» (European Union) uses a blue flag with 12 yellow stars in a circle. The number 12 does not change when new countries join: it is a symbol of unity. Spain has been a member of the European Union since 1986.

1031.texto: In municipal elections, people vote for…
1031.explicacion: In municipal elections, people vote for local councillors («concejales») on party lists. Then the councillors elect the mayor («alcalde»). So the answer is «alcaldes y concejales». Ministers are not elected this way, and deputies and senators are chosen in general elections.
1031.nota: For the exam, the manual's answer counts, although in reality people vote directly only for councillors, who then elect the mayor.

1032.texto: Which language is official in the País Vasco (Basque Country)?
1032.explicacion: In the Basque Country, Spanish and «euskera» (Basque) are official. «Bable» is spoken in Asturias and «aragonés» in Aragon, but they are not co-official languages. Tip: «Euskadi» and «euskera» start the same way.

1033.texto: All Spaniards have the duty to know the State's…
1033.explicacion: The Constitution says that Castilian Spanish is the «lengua oficial del Estado» (official language of the State). All Spaniards have the duty to know it and the right to use it. Regional languages are co-official only in their own autonomous communities.

1034.texto: Aranese is a co-official language spoken in a small area of…
1034.explicacion: «Aranés» (Aranese) is a variety of Occitan. It is spoken in the «Valle de Arán» (Aran Valley), in the Pyrenees of «Cataluña» (Catalonia), where it is official. It is not spoken in La Rioja or Aragon. Tip: Arán, aranés, Cataluña.

1035.texto: The institutions of an autonomous community are: the governing council, the president and…
1035.explicacion: Each autonomous community has three institutions: the governing council, the president and the «asamblea legislativa» (legislative assembly), its parliament that passes regional laws. The «ayuntamiento» runs a single municipality, and the «delegación del Gobierno» represents the State. Tip: government, president, parliament.

1036.texto: Which of these options is a co-official language in an autonomous community?
1036.explicacion: «Gallego» (Galician) is co-official in Galicia, alongside Spanish. Aragonese is protected in Aragon, but it is not co-official. Murcian is not a separate language: it is a regional way of speaking Spanish. Tip: «Galicia», «gallego».

1037.texto: Which institution aims to promote the teaching of the Spanish language and spread culture in Spanish?
opciones: El Instituto Nacional de Administración Pública (National Institute of Public Administration).
El Instituto Nacional de Estadística (National Statistics Institute).
1037.explicacion: The «Instituto Cervantes» promotes the teaching of Spanish and culture in Spanish around the world, with centres in many countries. It also runs this CCSE exam. The Statistics Institute produces statistics, and the INAP trains civil servants.

1038.texto: Which of the following bodies works to achieve linguistic standardisation?
opciones: The Real Academia Española (Royal Spanish Academy).
1038.explicacion: The «Real Academia Española» sets the rules of Spanish: spelling, grammar and the dictionary, so that everyone uses the language in a common way. The Instituto Cervantes teaches Spanish abroad, and the Institut Ramon Llull promotes Catalan. Tip: Academy means rules.
1038.nota: For the exam, the manual's answer (the RAE) counts, although «normalización lingüística» is also used for promoting the co-official languages.

1039.texto: Where does the President of the Government live?
opciones: In the Palacio de la Zarzuela.
In the Palacio de la Moncloa.
1039.explicacion: The President of the Government lives and works in the «Palacio de la Moncloa» in Madrid. The king lives in the Palacio de la Zarzuela, and the Royal Palace is used for official ceremonies. Tip: «Moncloa» for the president, «Zarzuela» for the king.

1040.texto: Which of the following bodies is part of Spain's Armed Forces?
1040.explicacion: The Armed Forces are the Army, the Navy («Armada») and the «Ejército del Aire» (Air Force). The «Guardia Civil» is a security force of military nature, but it is not part of the Armed Forces. The «Policía Foral» is the police of Navarre.
1040.nota: For the exam, the answer is «El Ejército del Aire», although since 2022 its official name is Ejército del Aire y del Espacio.

1041.texto: Who is part of the Government?
1041.explicacion: The Government is made up of the president, the vice-presidents if there are any, and the ministers («los ministros»). Each minister runs a ministry, such as Health or Education. Mayors and councillors work in the town council («ayuntamiento»), not in the Government of Spain.

opciones: social and democratic State under the rule of law.
1042.explicacion: Article 1 of the Constitution says Spain is an «estado social y democrático de Derecho». Social: it protects people's welfare. Democratic: the people choose. Rule of law: everyone must obey the law. The other two forms do not describe Spain.

1043.texto: Which of these acronyms belongs to a political party?
1043.explicacion: «PP» stands for «Partido Popular», a Spanish political party. «PIB» means gross domestic product (GDP), an economic figure. «UE» means European Union (EU), an organisation of countries. Tip: the first P in PP stands for «partido» (party).

1044.texto: What title does the future queen, the king's daughter, hold?
1044.explicacion: The heir to the Crown holds the title «Princesa de Asturias» (Princess of Asturias). Today this is Leonor, the eldest daughter of King Felipe VI. A male heir is called Prince of Asturias. Duchess of Alba is a noble title.

1045.texto: Under which king was democracy restored in Spain after the Franco regime?
1045.explicacion: Franco died in 1975 and «Juan Carlos I» was proclaimed king. During his reign came the «Transición» (transition to democracy) and the 1978 Constitution, which restored democracy. Charles III reigned in the 18th century, and Alfonso XIII before the Second Republic.

1046.texto: In what year was the Spanish Constitution approved?
1046.explicacion: The Spanish Constitution was approved in 1978. Citizens voted for it in a referendum on 6 December that year. That is why 6 December is the «Día de la Constitución» (Constitution Day), a national holiday. Tip: 6 December 1978.

1047.texto: How many autonomous communities have their own flag?
opciones: Those that have a co-official language.
1047.explicacion: «Todas»: all the autonomous communities have their own flag, set out in their «Estatuto de Autonomía» (Statute of Autonomy). It flies next to the Spanish flag on their official buildings. It does not depend on language: Andalusia and Madrid have flags too.

1048.texto: Which official body handles citizens' complaints about public administrations working badly?
opciones: The Oficina de Atención al Consumidor (Consumer Office).
1048.explicacion: The «Defensor del Pueblo» (Ombudsman) protects people's rights in their dealings with public administrations. If a public service works badly, you can file a complaint for free. The Consumer Office helps with shopping problems, and the National Police deals with security.

1049.texto: What is the minimum number of signatures citizens must collect to present a bill?
1049.explicacion: To present an «iniciativa legislativa popular» (popular legislative initiative), you need at least 500,000 signatures from citizens with the right to vote. With these signatures, the bill reaches the Congress. Tip: half a million, the largest number of the three options.

1050.texto: Which of the following international organisations does Spain belong to?
1050.explicacion: Spain has been a member of the «Fondo Monetario Internacional» (FMI, International Monetary Fund) since 1958. The IMF helps keep the world economy stable. The CIS and the Eurasian Economic Union group countries of the former Soviet Union, and Spain is not part of them.

1051.texto: In the organisation of the Administration, there are three levels: central, regional (autonómica) and…
1051.explicacion: Spain's public administration has three levels: central (the State), autonomous (the «comunidades autónomas») and local (town councils or «ayuntamientos», provincial councils and island councils). «Estatal» means the same as central, so it is not a separate level. Tip: State, region, town, from biggest to smallest; the answer is «local».

1052.explicacion: Legislative power makes the laws, and it belongs to the «Cortes Generales», made up of deputies («diputados») and senators («senadores»). The president and ministers are the Government, which is executive power. Judges and magistrates are judicial power. Tip: «legislativo» comes from «ley», meaning law.

opciones: In the Palacio de la Moneda.
In the Palacio de la Zarzuela.
In the Palacio de la Moncloa.
1053.explicacion: The King of Spain lives in the «Palacio de la Zarzuela», in Madrid. «La Moncloa» is the residence of the Prime Minister (president of the Government). «La Moneda» is in Santiago, Chile, and belongs to the Chilean president. Tip: «Zarzuela» for the King, «Moncloa» for the Prime Minister.

1054.texto: The official name of the Spanish parliament is…
opciones: Congreso de los Diputados (Chamber of Deputies).
1054.explicacion: The official name of the Spanish parliament is «Cortes Generales». It has two chambers: the «Congreso de los Diputados» and the «Senado». Each one is only a part, not the name of the whole parliament. Tip: the «Cortes Generales» are the whole; Congress and Senate are its two halves.

1055.texto: The Spanish Institute for Foreign Trade, the Women's Institute and the Directorate-General for Traffic (Dirección General de Tráfico)…
1055.explicacion: According to the manual, these three bodies «dependen de ministerios»: each one is attached to a specific ministry. They are not international bodies, because they are Spanish. Tip: the traffic authority («Tráfico») depends on the Ministry of the Interior.
1055.nota: For the exam, the answer is «dependen de ministerios», although legally some of them are also autonomous bodies attached to a ministry.

1056.explicacion: In Spain, «tanto los hombres como las mujeres» can reign. The Constitution allows it, although in the line of succession a son comes before a daughter. In fact, the current heir is a woman: Princess «Leonor». Tip: Leonor will be queen, so both men and women can reign.

1057.texto: The Court of Audit (Tribunal de Cuentas) depends on…
opciones: the Office of the Prime Minister (Presidencia del Gobierno).
1057.explicacion: The «Tribunal de Cuentas» checks how public money is spent, and it depends directly on the «Cortes Generales». It does not depend on the Government or the Ministry of Finance, because its job is to check the Government. Tip: whoever watches the Government's money reports to Parliament.

1058.texto: Who is the third authority of the State, after the King and the Prime Minister (president of the Government)?
opciones: The president of the Congreso de los Diputados (Chamber of Deputies).
1058.explicacion: In the official order of precedence, after the King and the Prime Minister comes the «presidente del Congreso de los Diputados». The president of the Senate is fourth, and a minister comes after them. Tip: the Congress is the more powerful chamber, so its president goes first.

1059.texto: Which co-official language is spoken in the Balearic Islands (Islas Baleares)?
1059.explicacion: In the Balearic Islands, the official languages are Castilian Spanish and Catalan («catalán»). «Gallego» is spoken in Galicia, and «euskera» in the Basque Country and part of Navarre. Tip: the Balearics are close to Catalonia and Valencia, so Catalan is spoken there.

1060.texto: The Constitution upholds values such as freedom, equality, political pluralism and…
1060.explicacion: Article 1 of the Constitution lists four higher values: freedom, justice («la justicia»), equality and political pluralism. Solidarity appears in other articles, but not in this list. Fraternity is part of France's motto, not Spain's. Tip: remember the Spanish initials L, J, I, P (libertad, justicia, igualdad, pluralismo).

1061.texto: Once a law has been passed, what does it need in order to be applied?
1061.explicacion: According to the manual, many laws need «normas que la desarrollen» after they are passed: implementing rules such as the Government's regulations («reglamentos»). These rules set out the details so the law can work in practice. Parliament does not review it again. Tip: the law gives the general idea, the regulation gives the details.
1061.nota: For the exam, the answer is «Normas que la desarrollen», although in reality many laws apply directly once they are published in the «BOE» and come into force.

1062.texto: How many inhabitants does Spain have?
1062.explicacion: Spain has about «49 millones» (49 million) inhabitants, according to the latest figures from the «INE», the national statistics office. 67 million is roughly the population of France or the United Kingdom, and 95 million is far too many. Tip: Spain is just under 50 million.

1063.texto: Which of these is an advisory body of the Spanish Government?
opciones: The Consejo de Estado (Council of State).
1063.explicacion: The «Consejo de Estado» is the Government's highest advisory body: it gives its opinion before some important decisions. The European Parliament belongs to the European Union, and the «Tribunal Constitucional» is a court, not an adviser. Tip: «consejo» means advice.

1064.texto: Who directs Spain's domestic and foreign policy?
opciones: The Congreso de los Diputados (Chamber of Deputies).
1064.explicacion: «El Gobierno» (the Government) directs domestic and foreign policy, the Administration and the defence of the State. The King represents Spain but does not govern. Congress makes laws and controls the Government, but does not direct it. Tip: «Gobierno» comes from «gobernar», to govern.

1065.texto: The Ombudsman (Defensor del Pueblo) depends on…
opciones: the Tribunal de Cuentas (Court of Audit).
1065.explicacion: The «Defensor del Pueblo» protects people's rights in their dealings with the Administration. It depends on the «Cortes Generales», which elect the Ombudsman. It does not depend on the Council of Ministers, because it sometimes has to check the Government. Tip: like the «Tribunal de Cuentas», it depends on Parliament.

1066.texto: The mission of the Etxepare Institute (Instituto Etxepare) is to promote…
1066.explicacion: The «Instituto Etxepare» promotes the Basque language («euskera») and Basque culture around the world. It is named after Bernart Etxepare, author of the first printed book in Basque. «Bable» is the language of Asturias, not Cantabria. Tip: the letters «tx» are typically Basque.

1067.texto: Which of these cities is among the 10 most populated in Spain?
1067.explicacion: «Málaga» is one of Spain's largest cities, with about 590,000 inhabitants, among the top six. «Cádiz» and «Albacete» are provincial capitals, but each has fewer than 200,000 inhabitants. Tip: Málaga is the big city of the «Costa del Sol».

1068.texto: Who can carry out online procedures with the Public Administration?
1068.explicacion: «Cualquier ciudadano» (any citizen) can do procedures online with the Administration, for example on the «sede electrónica» using a digital certificate or «Cl@ve». You do not need to be a judge or a lawyer. Tip: e-government is for everyone.

1069.texto: What is the name of the King of Spain?
1069.explicacion: The current King of Spain is «Felipe VI», since June 2014. «Juan Carlos I» is his father and reigned before him, from 1975 to 2014. «Alfonso XIII» was king in the early twentieth century. Tip: Felipe VI, number six; his daughter Leonor is the heir.

1070.texto: What is the name of the governing body of judges and magistrates?
opciones: Consejo General del Poder Judicial (General Council of the Judiciary).
1070.explicacion: The «Consejo General del Poder Judicial» is the governing body of judges and magistrates: it appoints them and organises and supervises their work. The «Tribunal Supremo» is the highest court, but it judges cases rather than governing judges. The «Consejo de Estado» advises the Government. Tip: its name already says «Poder Judicial».

1071.texto: Who approves the General State Budget?
opciones: The Tribunal de Cuentas (Court of Audit).
1071.explicacion: The Government prepares the General State Budget, but it is the «Cortes Generales» that approve it, through the votes of deputies and senators. Afterwards, the «Tribunal de Cuentas» checks how the money is spent. Tip: the Government proposes, Parliament approves, the Court of Audit checks.

1072.explicacion: The 1978 Constitution is Spain's «ley fundamental» (fundamental law): it is the highest rule, and all other laws must respect it. It is not part of another law, nor a secondary law. Tip: think of the foundations of a house; everything else rests on them.

1073.texto: The Cortes Generales (Parliament) are made up of the Senado (Senate) and…
opciones: the Congreso de los Diputados (Chamber of Deputies).
the Consejo de Estado (Council of State).
1073.explicacion: The «Cortes Generales» have two chambers: the «Congreso de los Diputados» and the «Senado». The «Tribunal Supremo» belongs to the judiciary, and the «Consejo de Estado» advises the Government, so neither is part of Parliament. Tip: deputies sit in Congress, senators in the Senate.

1074.explicacion: «El poder legislativo» (legislative power), that is, the «Cortes Generales», drafts and passes laws. Executive power is the Government, which governs and applies the laws. Judicial power is the judges, who decide cases according to the laws. Tip: «legislativo» comes from «ley», law.

1075.texto: Defending Spain's territorial integrity is the responsibility of…
opciones: the National Police and the Guardia Civil (Civil Guard).
the National Police and the regional police forces.
1075.explicacion: Under Article 8 of the Constitution, «las Fuerzas Armadas» (the Armed Forces: Army, Navy, and Air and Space Force) defend Spain's territorial integrity and sovereignty. The National Police, the «Guardia Civil» and regional police forces protect public safety. Tip: borders and territory belong to the Armed Forces.

1076.texto: Since 1989, the Spanish Army has taken part in peace missions of the…
opciones: Organización de Estados Iberoamericanos (OEI) (Organization of Ibero-American States).
Organización de las Naciones Unidas (ONU) (United Nations).
1076.explicacion: Since 1989, Spanish troops have joined peace missions of the «Organización de las Naciones Unidas (ONU)», the United Nations, for example in Lebanon. The OEI works on education and culture, and the UEO no longer exists. Tip: peace missions around the world, blue helmets, ONU.

1077.texto: Who guards ports and airports, borders and coasts?
1077.explicacion: The «Guardia Civil» guards the coasts, borders, ports and airports. It also controls traffic on the roads and works mainly in rural areas. The «Policía local» only works inside its own town. Tip: the Guardia Civil guards the edges of Spain.

1078.texto: Who carries out passport control at Spain's borders?
1078.explicacion: The «Policía Nacional» checks passports and documents at the borders. It also issues the DNI and the passport and controls the entry of foreigners. The Guardia Civil watches the border area, but the documents are checked by the Policía Nacional.

1079.texto: Which of these politicians has been President of the Government (Prime Minister) of Spain?
1079.explicacion: «José María Aznar» was President of the Government of Spain from 1996 to 2004. Manuel Fraga was a minister and later president of the Xunta de Galicia (Galician regional government). Yolanda Díaz has been a deputy prime minister, but never head of the Government.

1080.texto: What is the name of the regional police of Catalonia?
1080.explicacion: The regional police of Catalonia is called the «Mossos d'Esquadra». The «Ertzaintza» is the police of the Basque Country, and the «Guardia Civil» works across the whole State. Tip: «Mossos» is a Catalan word, and Catalonia has its own language.

1081.texto: What is the name of the regional police of the Basque Country?
1081.explicacion: The regional police of the Basque Country is called the «Ertzaintza». It is a word in euskera, the Basque language. The «Mossos d'Esquadra» are the police of Catalonia, and the «Guardia Civil» works all over Spain. Tip: Ertzaintza starts with E, like Euskadi.

1082.texto: Since what year has Felipe VI been king?
1082.explicacion: Felipe VI has been king «desde 2014» (since 2014), when his father, Juan Carlos I, abdicated. Juan Carlos I had been king since 1975, after Franco's death. Nothing changed in the Crown in 2020. Tip: 2014 is the year of the abdication.

1083.texto: Who directs traffic in towns and cities?
1083.explicacion: The «Policía Local» belongs to the town council (ayuntamiento) and directs traffic inside towns and cities. The Guardia Civil watches traffic on the roads outside the cities. Protección Civil helps in emergencies and disasters. Tip: local means your own town or city.

1084.texto: Who can file a complaint with the Defensor del Pueblo (Ombudsman)?
1084.explicacion: The «Defensor del Pueblo» (Ombudsman) protects people's rights against the public administration. «Todos los ciudadanos, españoles o extranjeros» (all citizens, Spanish or foreign) can file a complaint, whatever their age or legal status. Complaints are free and you do not need a lawyer.

1085.texto: In Spain, voting in elections is…
1085.explicacion: In Spain, voting in elections is «un derecho» (a right), not an obligation. Each person decides whether to vote, and there is no fine for not voting. That is why the other two options are wrong: nobody is forced to vote. Tip: voting is free and voluntary.

1086.texto: Who monitors traffic on the roads?
1086.explicacion: The «Guardia Civil» monitors traffic on the roads outside cities. It has a special traffic unit with motorbikes and patrol cars. The Policía Nacional does not do this job, and the Army is in charge of defence. Tip: road, Guardia Civil; city, Policía Local.

1087.texto: Which body is in charge of collecting taxes?
opciones: The Tribunal de Cuentas (Court of Auditors).
The Consejo Económico y Social (Economic and Social Council).
1087.explicacion: The «Agencia Tributaria» (Tax Agency) collects State taxes, such as IRPF (income tax) and IVA (VAT). The Tribunal de Cuentas checks how public money is spent, and the Consejo Económico y Social gives opinions on economic and labour matters. Tip: tributo means tax.

opciones: In the bulletin of the Instituto Nacional de Estadística (INE) (National Statistics Institute).
On the Portal de la Administración Electrónica (PAe) (e-Government Portal).
In the Boletín Oficial del Estado (BOE) (Official State Gazette).
1088.explicacion: National laws are published in the «Boletín Oficial del Estado (BOE)», the Official State Gazette. A law comes into force after it appears in the BOE, which anyone can read online for free. The INE produces statistics and the PAe gives information about e-government.

1089.texto: What are the governing bodies that exist only in the Canary Islands called?
1089.explicacion: The «Cabildos» govern each island and exist only in the Canary Islands. In the Balearic Islands, the similar body is called «Consejo insular». The «Diputaciones» govern provinces in other parts of Spain. Tip: Canarias and Cabildos both start with C.

1090.texto: Which of these administrative procedures can be done on the official website (sede electrónica)?
1090.explicacion: On the Tax Agency's «sede electrónica» (official website), you can «pagar los impuestos» (pay taxes) online without going to an office. To get a DNI or renew a passport, however, you must go in person to the Policía Nacional, because they take your fingerprint and photo.

1091.texto: What is the information phone number of the General State Administration (Administración General del Estado)?
1091.explicacion: «060» is the information number of the Administración General del Estado (central government). 010 is an information number used by many town councils, and 091 is the number of the Policía Nacional. Tip: 060 for the State, 091 for the police.

1092.explicacion: Spain is organised into 17 «comunidades autónomas» (autonomous communities) and two autonomous cities, Ceuta and Melilla. It is not a federal state like Germany, and it has no cantons like Switzerland. Tip: think of autonomous communities such as Andalusia, Galicia or Madrid.

1093.texto: How many political parties are there in Spain?
1093.explicacion: Spain has «muchos» (many) political parties, because the Constitution recognises political pluralism. Any group of people can create a party if it respects the law and democracy. A country with only one party, or with no parties, would not be a democracy.

1094.texto: Where does the investiture of the President of the Government take place?
opciones: At the Palacio de la Moncloa (Moncloa Palace).
In the Congreso de los Diputados (Congress of Deputies).
1094.explicacion: The investiture of the President of the Government takes place «en el Congreso de los Diputados» (in the Congress of Deputies). The deputies vote on the candidate and, if he or she wins, the King appoints the new president. La Moncloa is the president's residence, and the Senate does not vote.

1095.texto: Who holds supreme command of the Armed Forces?
1095.explicacion: Under the Constitution, «el rey» (the King) holds supreme command of the Armed Forces. It is mainly a symbolic role: the Government directs defence policy and the Minister of Defence runs the ministry. Tip: the King is head of State and the first soldier.

1096.texto: Who is the representative of the State in an autonomous community?
opciones: The president of the autonomous community.
The president of the regional Assembly (Asamblea autonómica).
1096.explicacion: The «delegado del Gobierno» (Government Delegate) represents the Spanish Government in each autonomous community and runs the State administration there. The president of the community leads the regional government, and the president of the Asamblea chairs the regional parliament.
1096.nota: For the exam, the answer is «el delegado del Gobierno», although the Constitution also gives the president of the autonomous community the ordinary representation of the State in that territory.

1097.texto: How many provinces are there in Spain?
1097.explicacion: Spain has «50» provinces (provincias), spread across 17 autonomous communities. Some communities have only one province, like Madrid or Murcia, while Andalusia has eight. Ceuta and Melilla are autonomous cities on top of that. Tip: 50, a nice round number.

1098.texto: Teaching the co-official languages is the responsibility…
1098.explicacion: Teaching co-official languages, such as Catalan, Galician or Basque, is the responsibility «de la comunidad autónoma» (of the autonomous community). Each community with its own language decides how it is taught in schools. The State sets the basic rules for education, and provinces have no role here.

opciones: to the Government of the State.
to the Congreso (Congress) and the Senado (Senate).
1099.explicacion: Executive power belongs «al Gobierno del Estado» (to the Government of the State), made up of the president, the vice-presidents and the ministers. The Congreso and the Senado hold legislative power and make laws, and judges and magistrates hold judicial power. Tip: executive comes from execute, to govern.

1100.texto: How many chambers does the Spanish Parliament have?
1100.explicacion: The Spanish Parliament, called the «Cortes Generales», has «dos» (two) chambers: the «Congreso de los Diputados» (Congress of Deputies) and the «Senado» (Senate). That is why it is called a bicameral parliament. Tip: bi means two, as in bicycle, which has two wheels.

1101.texto: Water supply and street lighting in towns and cities are the responsibility of…
opciones: the Ministerio de Obras Públicas y Urbanismo (Ministry of Public Works and Urban Planning).
1101.explicacion: Water, street lighting and street cleaning are local services run by the town council, called «ayuntamiento» in Spain. The regional government and the national ministries deal with bigger matters. Tip: whatever you see in your own street is usually the job of your «ayuntamiento».

1102.texto: In matters such as nationality, immigration, emigration or the status of foreigners, the only one with authority is…
1102.explicacion: The Spanish Constitution gives the State, «el Estado», exclusive power over nationality, immigration, emigration and the status of foreigners. The autonomous communities and town councils cannot decide on these matters. That is why your nationality application is decided by the State, specifically by the Ministry of Justice.

1103.texto: How many women have been Prime Minister (presidenta del Gobierno) of Spain?
1103.explicacion: So far, no woman has been Prime Minister of Spain. Several women have served as Deputy Prime Minister or as ministers, but never as head of the Government. Do not confuse president with vice-president: the answer is «Ninguna», which means none.

1104.texto: International relations are the responsibility of…
1104.explicacion: Under the Constitution, international relations are an exclusive power of the State, «el Estado». Autonomous communities and town councils cannot sign treaties with other countries. Tip: Spain speaks to the rest of the world with one single voice, and that voice is the State.

1105.texto: The town council (Ayuntamiento) is made up of the mayor and…
1105.explicacion: The town council, «ayuntamiento», is made up of the mayor, «alcalde», and the councillors, «concejales», whom residents elect in municipal elections. Members of Parliament and senators work in the Cortes Generales, not in the town council. Tip: the mayor and the «concejales» run your town or city.

1106.texto: Who forms the government of the autonomous communities?
opciones: The president and the regional ministers (consejeros).
1106.explicacion: Each autonomous community has a Governing Council formed by its president and regional ministers, «el presidente y los consejeros». Ministers belong to the Government of Spain, and the mayor and councillors belong to the town council. Tip: the State has «ministros», while the autonomous community has «consejeros».

1107.texto: What is the governing body of municipalities?
1107.explicacion: A municipality, «municipio», is governed by its town council, «ayuntamiento», with the mayor and councillors. The «diputación» governs a province and the «cabildo» governs each island in the Canary Islands. Tip: «municipio» goes with «ayuntamiento», and «provincia» goes with «diputación».

1108.texto: What are the governing bodies of Spanish provinces called?
1108.explicacion: Spanish provinces are governed by provincial councils, called «diputaciones provinciales». The «cabildos» govern the Canary Islands and the «consejos insulares» govern the Balearic Islands, so they run islands, not provinces. Tip: «provincia» always goes with «diputación».

1109.texto: What is the highest body of executive power?
1109.explicacion: The Government, «el Gobierno», leads the executive power: it applies the laws and runs the country's policy. The «Cortes Generales» hold legislative power and make the laws, while the Armed Forces defend Spain but do not govern. Tip: the executive executes, and that is the job of the Government.

1110.texto: The Spanish language is also called…
1110.explicacion: Spanish is also called Castilian, «castellano», because it was born in the region of Castile. The Constitution says that «castellano» is the official language of the State. Aragonese and Leonese are other historical languages of Spain, not another name for Spanish.

1111.texto: Who is elected in European Parliament elections?
1111.explicacion: In European Parliament elections, citizens elect Members of the European Parliament, «eurodiputados», who represent them in the European Union. Ministers are not elected at the ballot box, and managing directors run companies. Tip: «eurodiputados» simply combines «euro» and «diputados», meaning members of parliament.

1112.texto: Spanish citizens can vote from the age of…
1112.explicacion: In Spain you can vote from the age of 18, which is the age of majority under the Constitution. At 16 you still cannot vote in elections. Tip: 18, «18 años» in Spanish, is both the age when you become an adult and the age when you can vote.

1113.texto: Some foreign citizens can vote in the…
1113.explicacion: Some foreigners can vote in municipal elections, «municipales»: citizens of the European Union and citizens of countries with a reciprocity agreement with Spain. Only Spanish citizens can vote in regional and general elections. Tip: a foreign resident votes in the town where they live.

1114.texto: Who oversees the State's financial management?
opciones: The Banco de España (Bank of Spain).
The Tribunal de Cuentas (Court of Audit).
1114.explicacion: The «Tribunal de Cuentas», Spain's Court of Audit, checks how the State spends public money and oversees its financial management. The «Banco de España» supervises banks, and the «Agencia Tributaria» collects taxes. Tip: «cuentas» means accounts, and this court checks the public accounts.

1115.texto: Who is elected in general elections?
opciones: Senators and members of the Congress of Deputies.
1115.explicacion: In general elections, «elecciones generales», voters elect the members of the Congress of Deputies and most senators, «senadores y diputados». MEPs are chosen in European elections and councillors in municipal elections. Tip: general elections choose the «Cortes Generales», the Spanish Parliament.

1116.texto: How many members does the Congreso de los Diputados (Congress of Deputies) have?
1116.explicacion: The «Congreso de los Diputados» has 350 members. The Constitution allows between 300 and 400, and the electoral law sets the number at 350. Tip: think of 300 and 400 as the limits, with 350 sitting exactly in the middle.

1117.texto: Municipalities and provinces form part of the…
1117.explicacion: Municipalities and provinces make up the local administration, «Administración local», the one closest to residents. The regional administration belongs to the autonomous communities, and the central administration belongs to the State. Tip: «local» refers to the place where you live.

1118.texto: The most populated autonomous community in Spain is…
1118.explicacion: Andalusia, «Andalucía», is the autonomous community with the most inhabitants in Spain, with more than eight and a half million people. Catalonia is second and Madrid third. Castilla y León is very large in area, but it has a small population.

1119.texto: What is the organisation that defends workers' interests called?
1119.explicacion: A trade union, «sindicato», defends workers' rights, such as pay, working hours and working conditions. A political party stands in elections, and an association brings together people with a shared interest. Tip: «sindicato» sounds like syndicate, a group that acts together for its members.

1120.texto: Who elects the Prime Minister (presidente del Gobierno)?
opciones: The Congreso de los Diputados (Congress of Deputies).
1120.explicacion: The «Congreso de los Diputados» elects the Prime Minister in a vote called «investidura». The King proposes a candidate and then formally appoints them, but does not elect them, and the Supreme Court is a court of law. Tip: citizens elect the deputies, and the deputies elect the Prime Minister.

2001.texto: In Spain, the Constitution requires all citizens to practise a religion.
2001.explicacion: The Constitution guarantees freedom of religion: everyone may follow a religion or have no religion at all. Spain is also a non-denominational State, «aconfesional», which means there is no official religion. So the answer is «Falso» (false): nobody can be forced to practise any religion.

2002.texto: Spaniards who obtain nationality through residence must wait three years before they can vote in elections.
2002.explicacion: A person who obtains Spanish nationality through residence has the same rights as other Spaniards from that moment. They can vote in the next elections if they are registered on the electoral roll, the «censo electoral». So the answer is «Falso» (false): there is no three-year wait.

2003.texto: In Spain, the Constitution prohibits torture and the death penalty.
2003.explicacion: The Constitution protects the right to life and to physical integrity: it bans torture and inhuman or degrading treatment, and it declares the death penalty, «pena de muerte», abolished. So the answer is «Verdadero» (true): in Spain nobody can be tortured or sentenced to death.
2003.nota: For the exam the valid answer is «Verdadero»; note that the Constitution's text left an exception for military law in wartime, which a 1995 law removed.

2004.explicacion: The Constitution says that the internal structure and functioning of political parties must be democratic. Parties express political pluralism and help citizens take part in public life. So the answer is «Verdadero» (true). Tip: in a democracy, the parties themselves must also be democratic.

2005.texto: Someone can be forced to say what their political or religious ideas are.
2005.explicacion: The Constitution says that nobody can be forced to declare their ideology, religion or beliefs, «ideología, religión o creencias». Each person decides whether to talk about their ideas. So the answer is «Falso» (false). Tip: your ideas belong to you, and nobody can make you reveal them.

2006.texto: A person's right to enter and leave Spain freely can be restricted for ideological reasons.
2006.explicacion: The Constitution protects the freedom to enter and leave Spain, and also freedom of ideology («libertad ideológica»). Nobody can lose this right because of their political or religious ideas. So the answer is «Falso» (false): thinking differently is never a reason to restrict your travel.

2007.texto: Primary Education (from 6 to 12 years old) is free and compulsory.
2007.explicacion: In Spain, Primary Education («Educación Primaria») runs from age 6 to 12. It is compulsory for all children and free in public schools. So the answer is «Verdadero» (true). Tip: compulsory schooling starts at age 6, with the first year of Primaria.

2008.texto: The Constitution guarantees Spaniards the right to decent housing.
2008.explicacion: Article 47 of the Constitution says that all Spaniards have the right to enjoy decent housing («vivienda digna»). Public authorities must help make this possible, for example with subsidised housing. So the answer is «Verdadero» (true).
2008.nota: For the exam the answer is «Verdadero», but decent housing is a guiding principle for public authorities, not a right you can claim directly before a judge.

2009.texto: In Spain the police can enter any home without a court order at any time.
2009.explicacion: The home is inviolable («domicilio inviolable»). The police can only enter with the owner's permission, with a judge's order, or if a crime is being committed at that moment. So the answer is «Falso» (false): they cannot enter any home at any time.

2010.texto: The secrecy of Spaniards' communications is guaranteed, except by court order.
2010.explicacion: The Constitution protects the secrecy of communications («secreto de las comunicaciones»): letters, calls, messages and emails. Only a judge can authorise opening or listening to them. So the answer is «Verdadero» (true). Remember the rule: secret, «salvo resolución judicial» (unless a court decides).

2011.texto: The Constitution recognises citizens' right to associate freely.
2011.explicacion: The Constitution recognises the right of association («derecho de asociación»). People can freely create or join associations, such as neighbourhood, parents' or cultural associations. Nobody is forced to join one. So the answer is «Verdadero» (true).

2012.texto: Teachers can teach freely, within the limits of the Constitution.
2012.explicacion: The Constitution recognises academic freedom («libertad de cátedra»). Teachers can teach freely, but always respecting the Constitution and the rights of others. So the answer is «Verdadero» (true). Tip: «cátedra» means a teacher's chair or post.

2013.texto: The Constitution recognises only the fundamental rights of Spaniards.
2013.explicacion: Fundamental rights («derechos fundamentales») protect all people, not only Spaniards. Foreigners in Spain also have rights such as dignity, life and freedom, under the law. So the answer is «Falso» (false): the word «únicamente» (only) makes the sentence wrong.

2014.texto: Citizens must cooperate with judges if asked to.
2014.explicacion: The Constitution says everyone must cooperate with judges and courts («jueces y tribunales») when they ask, for example by appearing as a witness at a trial. So the answer is «Verdadero» (true): cooperating with justice is a duty.

2015.texto: The law limits third parties' access to personal data.
2015.explicacion: The Constitution asks the law to protect privacy and personal data («datos de carácter personal»). Other people or companies cannot use your name, address or health data without a legal reason. So the answer is «Verdadero» (true). This is called data protection («protección de datos»).

2016.texto: Freedom of the press is limited by respect for people's honour.
2016.explicacion: Freedom of expression and of the press is a right, but it has limits. It must respect people's honour («honor»), privacy and personal image. So the answer is «Verdadero» (true): a newspaper cannot invent lies to harm someone.

2017.texto: In Spain the grounds for separation and divorce are regulated by law.
2017.explicacion: The Constitution says the law regulates marriage, the rights of spouses and the grounds for separation and divorce («separación y divorcio»). So divorce exists and follows legal rules, such as the Civil Code («Código Civil»). The answer is «Verdadero» (true).

2018.texto: Free healthcare is only for people over 65.
2018.explicacion: Public healthcare («sanidad pública») in Spain is universal: it treats children, adults and older people, not only those over 65. It is paid for by everyone's taxes. So the answer is «Falso» (false). The word «solo» (only) often signals a false sentence.

2019.texto: In Spain men and women have the same rights.
2019.explicacion: Article 14 of the Constitution says all Spaniards are equal before the law («iguales ante la ley»). There can be no discrimination based on sex, race, religion or opinion. So the answer is «Verdadero» (true): men and women have the same rights.

2020.texto: Compulsory education has two stages: Primary Education and Compulsory Secondary Education.
2020.explicacion: In Spain, school is compulsory from age 6 to 16. There are two stages: Primary («Educación Primaria», ages 6 to 12) and Compulsory Secondary Education («ESO», ages 12 to 16). So the answer is «Verdadero» (true). Tip: «Primaria» plus «ESO».

2021.texto: In Spain there is an official religion.
2021.explicacion: Spain is a non-denominational state («Estado aconfesional»): no religion has state status. There is religious freedom, and everyone can follow any religion or none. The State cooperates with several faiths but has no official religion. So the answer is «Falso» (false).

2022.explicacion: Public healthcare («sanidad pública») in Spain is paid for through taxes. So visiting your family doctor, A&E or a public hospital costs nothing at the point of care. The answer is «Verdadero» (true). To use it you need a health card («tarjeta sanitaria»).
2022.nota: For the exam the answer is «Verdadero», although some services, such as prescription medicines, may involve a partial payment called «copago» (co-payment).

2023.texto: Basic education in Spain is only for foreigners.
2023.explicacion: Basic education («enseñanza básica») is a right and a duty for all children living in Spain, whether Spanish or foreign. It is compulsory and free in public schools. So the answer is «Falso» (false): it is not only for foreigners, it is for everyone.

2024.texto: In Spain the right of association is recognised.
2024.explicacion: Article 22 of the Constitution recognises the right of association («derecho de asociación»). People can form associations for lawful purposes, such as sports clubs, NGOs or migrant associations. Secret and paramilitary associations are banned. So the answer is «Verdadero» (true).

2025.texto: Trade unions can take part in negotiations with employers and with the Government.
2025.explicacion: Trade unions («sindicatos») defend workers' interests. They negotiate collective agreements («convenios colectivos») on pay and working hours with employers, and also talk with the Government about labour laws. So the answer is «Verdadero» (true). This is called social dialogue («diálogo social»).

2026.texto: Workers have the right to strike.
2026.explicacion: Article 28 of the Constitution recognises workers' right to strike («derecho de huelga») to defend their interests. During a strike, essential services such as hospitals or minimum transport («servicios mínimos») must continue. So the answer is «Verdadero» (true).

2027.texto: Freedom of ideology is guaranteed only in part of the national territory.
2027.explicacion: The Constitution guarantees freedom of ideology («libertad ideológica»), religion and worship throughout Spain. Fundamental rights are the same in all the autonomous communities («comunidades autónomas»). So the answer is «Falso» (false): it is not guaranteed in only part of the country.

2028.texto: All citizens have access to the public Social Security system, except if they are unemployed.
2028.explicacion: The public Social Security system («Seguridad Social») is for all citizens. It gives special protection in difficult situations such as unemployment («desempleo»), illness or retirement. So the answer is «Falso» (false): unemployed people also have access, for example through unemployment benefit.

2029.texto: Everyone has the right to enjoy an environment suitable for personal development, as well as the duty to preserve it.
2029.explicacion: Article 45 of the Constitution says everyone has the right to a suitable environment («medio ambiente adecuado») and also the duty to preserve it. It is both a right and an obligation: for example, not throwing rubbish in nature. So the answer is «Verdadero» (true).

2030.texto: In Spain, public authorities must protect health and promote sport.
2030.explicacion: The Constitution recognises the right to health protection («protección de la salud»). So public authorities («poderes públicos») run public healthcare and must also promote physical education and sport («deporte»). The answer is «Verdadero» (true). Tip: health and sport go together.

2031.texto: Basic education in Spain is compulsory and free.
2031.explicacion: The Spanish Constitution says that basic education («enseñanza básica») is compulsory and free. All children must go to school, and families do not pay for it in public schools. So the answer is «Verdadero». Tip: remember the words «obligatoria y gratuita», compulsory and free.

2032.texto: The law prohibits discrimination based on any personal or social circumstance.
2032.explicacion: The Constitution says that all Spaniards are equal before the law. No discrimination is allowed because of birth, race, sex, religion, opinion or any other «circunstancia personal o social». So the answer is «Verdadero». Tip: think of «igualdad», equality for everyone.

2033.texto: In Spain, citizens can move freely throughout the national territory.
2033.explicacion: The Constitution recognises freedom of movement («libertad de circulación»). Spaniards can travel and move freely around the whole country without asking for permission. They can also enter and leave Spain. So the answer is «Verdadero». Tip: «desplazarse libremente» means to move around freely.

2034.texto: Judges administer justice in Spain according to the Government's instructions.
2034.explicacion: Judges are independent («independientes»): they only follow the Constitution and the law, not the Government. This is the separation of powers in the State. So the sentence is wrong and the answer is «Falso». Tip: the Government governs and the judges judge, each one separately.

2035.texto: Spaniards must help in cases of catastrophe or public calamity.
2035.explicacion: The Constitution says that a law can set out citizens' duties in cases of serious risk, «catástrofe» or «calamidad pública». So in an emergency, Spaniards must cooperate and help. The answer is «Verdadero». Tip: in a disaster, everybody helps.

2036.texto: In Spain, citizens can choose which city they want to live in.
2036.explicacion: The Constitution recognises the right to freely choose your place of residence («residencia»). Each person decides which city or town to live in, without asking the State for permission. So the answer is «Verdadero». Tip: «residencia» is the place where you live, and you choose it.

opciones: In the Principality of Asturias (Principado de Asturias).
3001.explicacion: Cáceres and Badajoz are the two provinces of «Extremadura», in western Spain, next to Portugal. Asturias is in the north and Andalusia is in the south. Tip: Extremadura has only two provinces, Cáceres at the top and Badajoz at the bottom.

3002.texto: What is the capital of the Valencian Community (Comunidad Valenciana)?
3002.explicacion: The capital of the «Comunidad Valenciana» is the city of «Valencia», which has almost the same name as the region. Alicante and Castellón are the other two provinces, but they are not the capital. Tip: region «Valenciana», capital «Valencia».

3003.explicacion: The «islas Baleares» are in the «mar Mediterráneo», to the east of the peninsula. The main islands are Majorca, Minorca, Ibiza and Formentera. The Canary Islands are the ones in the Atlantic Ocean. Tip: Balearics in the Mediterranean, Canaries in the Atlantic.

3004.texto: What is the large plain in the centre of the Iberian Peninsula called?
3004.explicacion: The «Meseta» is a large high plain, a plateau, that covers the centre of the Iberian Peninsula. A «cordillera» is a mountain range and a «marisma» is a marsh near the coast. Tip: Madrid is on the «Meseta», right in the centre.

3005.explicacion: «Ordesa y Monte Perdido» National Park is in the Pyrenees, in «Aragón», in the province of Huesca. It is one of the oldest national parks in Spain. Tip: «Ordesa» and «Aragón» both start with a vowel and are both in the Pyrenees.

3006.texto: In which autonomous community are Guadalajara and Cuenca?
opciones: In Castile and León (Castilla y León).
3006.explicacion: Guadalajara and Cuenca are provinces of «Castilla-La Mancha», like Toledo, Ciudad Real and Albacete. Do not confuse it with «Castilla y León», which is further north. Tip: Cuenca and Guadalajara are east of Madrid, in La Mancha.

3007.texto: Which autonomous community has Santiago de Compostela as its capital?
3007.explicacion: «Santiago de Compostela» is the capital of «Galicia», in north-west Spain. It is famous for its cathedral and for the Way of Saint James. The capital of Asturias is Oviedo and the capital of Cantabria is Santander. Tip: the «Camino de Santiago» ends in Galicia.

3008.explicacion: Almería is one of the eight provinces of «Andalucía», in the south-east, on the Mediterranean Sea. The others are Huelva, Seville, Cádiz, Córdoba, Málaga, Jaén and Granada. The Canary Islands and Aragon have no province with this name. Tip: Almería, sunshine and Andalusia.

3009.texto: The capital of the autonomous community of Galicia is…
3009.explicacion: The capital of Galicia is «Santiago de Compostela», even though «A Coruña» and Vigo are bigger cities. The Galician Parliament and Government are in Santiago. Tip: the capital is not always the biggest city; in Galicia, the capital is Santiago.

3010.texto: Which of these rivers flows into the Mediterranean Sea?
3010.explicacion: The «Júcar» rises in the Serranía de Cuenca and flows into the «mar Mediterráneo», in the Valencian Community. The Tagus and the Douro flow west and reach the Atlantic Ocean in Portugal. Tip: Júcar, Valencia and the Mediterranean.

3011.explicacion: «Aneto» is the highest mountain in the «Pirineos», at about 3,400 metres. It is in the province of Huesca, in Aragon, near France. Sierra Nevada has the Mulhacén, the highest peak on the peninsula. Tip: Aneto and the Pyrenees are both in the north.

3012.texto: The city of Vitoria is the administrative seat of…
3012.explicacion: «Vitoria-Gasteiz» is home to the Parliament and the Government of the «País Vasco», so it is considered its capital. Pamplona is the capital of Navarre and Logroño is the capital of La Rioja. Tip: Vitoria, in Álava, is the Basque administrative centre.

opciones: autonomous communities and cities (comunidades y ciudades autónomas).
3013.explicacion: Spain is organised into 17 «comunidades autónomas» and 2 «ciudades autónomas», Ceuta and Melilla. Departments and districts are divisions used in other countries, such as France. Tip: in Spain everything is autonomous, 17 communities plus 2 cities.

3014.explicacion: «Aigüestortes» and Sant Maurici Lake National Park is in the Pyrenees, in «Cataluña», in the province of Lleida. Its name is in Catalan and means twisted waters. Tip: if the name sounds Catalan, think of Catalonia.

3015.texto: In North Africa there are Ceuta and…
3015.explicacion: «Ceuta» and «Melilla» are two Spanish autonomous cities in North Africa, on the coast of Morocco. Almería and Cádiz are in Andalusia, on the peninsula. Tip: Ceuta and Melilla, the two autonomous cities, always go together.

3016.texto: Where in Spain is there a climate with cold winters and very hot summers?
3016.explicacion: «Madrid» is in the centre of the peninsula, far from the sea, and has a continental climate: «inviernos fríos y veranos muy calurosos». The Canary Islands are mild all year and the Valencian Community has a milder Mediterranean climate. Tip: far from the sea means colder winters and hotter summers.

3017.texto: Which of these rivers flows into the Atlantic Ocean?
3017.explicacion: The «Guadalquivir» flows through Córdoba and Seville and reaches the «océano Atlántico» in the Gulf of Cádiz. The Júcar flows into the Mediterranean, and the Manzanares is a small river in Madrid that does not reach the sea. Tip: Guadalquivir, Seville, Atlantic.

3018.texto: Which of these provinces is part of the Community of Castile and León (Castilla y León)?
3018.explicacion: «Burgos» is one of the nine provinces of «Castilla y León», along with León, Valladolid, Salamanca and others. Huesca is in Aragon and Guadalajara is in Castile-La Mancha. Tip: Burgos, with its great Gothic cathedral, belongs to Castile and León.

3019.texto: In which autonomous community is the city of Huesca?
3019.explicacion: Huesca is one of the three provinces of «Aragón», together with Zaragoza and Teruel. It is in the north, near the Pyrenees. Castile-La Mancha and Extremadura are further south. Tip: Aragon has three provinces, from north to south: Huesca, Zaragoza and Teruel.

3020.texto: The Canary Islands (Canarias) have a climate that is…
3020.explicacion: The Canary Islands lie in the Atlantic Ocean, close to Africa. Their climate is «subtropical»: mild temperatures all year round and little rain. The «mediterráneo» climate belongs to the east coast and the «oceánico» climate to the north. Tip: people call them the islands of eternal spring.

3021.texto: The main river that flows into the Mediterranean Sea is the…
3021.explicacion: The «Ebro» rises in Cantabria and flows into the Mediterranean Sea near Tarragona, where it forms a large delta. The «Duero» and the «Tajo» flow west and reach the Atlantic Ocean in Portugal. Tip: the «Ebro» and the Mediterranean are both in the east.

3022.texto: Spain is among the most … countries in Europe.
3022.explicacion: Spain has many mountain ranges and a large central plateau, so it is one of the most «montañosos» countries in Europe. Think of the Pyrenees, Sierra Nevada or the Picos de Europa. It is not among the rainiest or the coldest countries: it is known for its sunshine.

3023.texto: In which province is the Monfragüe National Park?
3023.explicacion: «Monfragüe» National Park is in Extremadura, in the province of «Cáceres». It is famous for its birds, such as vultures, eagles and black storks. Ciudad Real has Cabañeros and Las Tablas de Daimiel, while Murcia has no national park at all.

3024.texto: What is the capital of the autonomous community of Extremadura?
3024.explicacion: The capital of Extremadura is «Mérida». Cáceres and Badajoz are the capitals of the region's two provinces, and Badajoz is the largest city, but neither is the regional capital. Tip: «Mérida» has a famous Roman theatre; it was the ancient city of Emerita Augusta.

4001.texto: The main characters of the novel Don Quixote (el Quijote) are Don Quixote and…
4001.explicacion: «el Quijote» is the great novel by Miguel de Cervantes. Don Quixote is a dreamy knight and «Sancho Panza» is his squire, a simple and practical man. Don Juan and Doña Inés belong to a different work: Don Juan Tenorio, by José Zorrilla.

4002.texto: Which Spanish scientist is recognised for her research?
4002.explicacion: «Margarita Salas» was a leading Spanish scientist in biochemistry and molecular biology. She discovered a protein from a virus that makes it easy and fast to copy DNA. Almudena Grandes was a novelist and Montserrat Caballé was an opera singer.

4003.texto: Who wrote The House of Bernarda Alba (La casa de Bernarda Alba)?
4003.explicacion: «La casa de Bernarda Alba» is a play by «Federico García Lorca», a poet and playwright from Granada. It tells the story of a very strict, controlling mother and her five daughters. Cervantes wrote Don Quixote, and Antonio Machado was mainly a poet.

4004.texto: Who wrote Nada, a novel about the Spanish post-war period?
4004.explicacion: «Carmen Laforet» wrote «Nada» when she was very young. The novel tells the story of a girl in the poor, gloomy Barcelona of the post-war years, and it won the first «Premio Nadal». Tip: «Nada» and «Nadal» start the same way.

4005.texto: Which musician composed Love, the Magician (El amor brujo)?
4005.explicacion: «Manuel de Falla», a composer from Cádiz, wrote «El amor brujo», which includes the famous Ritual Fire Dance. He also composed The Three-Cornered Hat. Isaac Albéniz wrote the Iberia suite and Joaquín Rodrigo wrote the Concierto de Aranjuez.

4006.texto: What is typical on Saint John's Eve (Noche de San Juan)?
4006.explicacion: «Noche de San Juan» is the night of 23 June, near the start of summer. The tradition is to light «hogueras» (bonfires) and jump over the flames, especially on beaches and in squares. Grapes are eaten on New Year's Eve, and books are given on Sant Jordi, 23 April.

4007.texto: What is the most characteristic instrument of flamenco music?
4007.explicacion: The «guitarra» is the most typical flamenco instrument, together with singing, dancing and hand clapping. The «gaita» (bagpipe) is typical of Galicia and Asturias, and the piano is not a traditional flamenco instrument. Tip: think of Paco de Lucía and his guitar.

4008.explicacion: «Isabel Coixet» is a «directora de cine» (film director) born in Barcelona. She has won several Goya Awards with films such as The Secret Life of Words and The Bookshop. Tip: Coixet makes films; she does not sing pop or dance ballet.

4009.texto: One of the most famous Spanish singers today is…
4009.explicacion: «Rosalía» is a Catalan singer who is very famous around the world today. She mixes flamenco with pop and urban music, and she has won Grammy Awards. Marisol and Lola Flores were very popular many years ago, in the twentieth century.

4010.texto: In which Spanish city is there a mosque that is a World Heritage Site?
4010.explicacion: The Mosque-Cathedral of «Córdoba» has been a World Heritage Site since 1984. It was built in the time of Al-Andalus and is famous for its red and white arches. Santiago de Compostela has a great cathedral, not a mosque.

4011.texto: In which Spanish city is the Alhambra (La Alhambra), a World Heritage Site?
4011.explicacion: The «Alhambra» is in «Granada». It is a group of palaces and gardens from the Nasrid period, the last Muslim kingdom on the peninsula. Tip to avoid mixing them up: Granada has the Alhambra, Córdoba has the Mosque and Seville has the Giralda.

4012.texto: What is the name of the Spanish director known for her critical eye and for modernising the country's cinema?
4012.explicacion: «Pilar Miró» was a film and television director. She made films such as El crimen de Cuenca and, while working in government, she promoted laws that modernised Spanish cinema. Sara Baras is a flamenco dancer and Penélope Cruz is an actress.

4013.texto: Which successful novel has Irene Vallejo written?
opciones: El infinito en un junco (Papyrus: The Invention of Books in the Ancient World).
El tiempo entre costuras (The Time in Between).
4013.explicacion: «Irene Vallejo», a writer from Zaragoza, wrote «El infinito en un junco», a hugely successful book about the history of books in the ancient world. El tiempo entre costuras is by María Dueñas and El camino is by Miguel Delibes.
4013.nota: For the exam the correct answer is «El infinito en un junco», although it is actually an essay, not a novel.

4014.texto: What is the name of the largest public institution devoted to research in Spain?
opciones: Consejo Superior de Investigaciones Científicas (CSIC) (Spanish National Research Council).
Sociedad General de Autores (SGAE) (General Society of Authors).
4014.explicacion: The «Consejo Superior de Investigaciones Científicas» («CSIC») is the largest public research institution in Spain. The RAE looks after the Spanish language, and the SGAE protects the rights of authors and musicians. Tip: the last C in CSIC stands for «Científicas» (scientific).

4015.texto: Paco de Lucía was a famous…
4015.explicacion: «Paco de Lucía» was a «guitarrista» (guitarist) born in Algeciras, in the province of Cádiz. He took flamenco guitar all over the world and mixed it with jazz and other styles. One of his best-known pieces is Entre dos aguas. He was not a scientist or a painter.

4016.texto: What do we celebrate on 24 December?
4016.explicacion: 24 December is «Nochebuena», Christmas Eve, the night before Christmas Day. Many families have dinner together that night. Carnival is in February or March, and San Juan is in June. Tip: «Nochebuena» is the 24th and «Nochevieja» (New Year's Eve) is 31 December.

4017.texto: Juan Mari Arzak is a famous…
4017.explicacion: «Juan Mari Arzak» is a Basque «cocinero» (chef) from San Sebastián. His restaurant, Arzak, has three Michelin stars, and he was one of the creators of new Basque cuisine. Tip: San Sebastián is famous for its food and its «pintxos».

4018.explicacion: «Clara Campoamor» was a lawyer and member of parliament. She defended the «derechos de la mujer» (women's rights) and made sure the 1931 Constitution gave women the right to vote in Spain. That is why she is a symbol of women's suffrage.

4019.texto: What typical songs are sung at Christmas?
4019.explicacion: «Villancicos» are the traditional Christmas carols, such as Los peces en el río. People sing them at home, in the street and at school. Flamenco is an art from Andalusia, and the «jota» is a folk dance and song from Aragon and other regions.

4020.texto: La Liga and the Copa del Rey (King's Cup) are … competitions.
4020.explicacion: «La Liga» is Spain's national «fútbol» (football) championship, and the «Copa del Rey» is the country's other big football tournament. Many teams play in both competitions during the season. Tip: Liga and Copa del Rey always mean football.

4021.texto: Who has received the Nobel Prize in Literature?
4021.explicacion: The Spanish poet «Vicente Aleixandre» won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1977. María Zambrano was a philosopher and Pablo Picasso was a painter, so neither won this prize. Tip: the literature prize goes to writers, and Aleixandre wrote poetry.

4022.texto: Which festival is celebrated in Pamplona on 7 July?
4022.explicacion: «Los sanfermines» is the big festival of Pamplona, in Navarre. It starts on 6 July, and 7 July is San Fermín's day. «Las Fallas» are in Valencia and the «Feria de Abril» is in Seville. Tip: Pamplona, July, running of the bulls.

4023.texto: Teresa Perales and Daniel Molina are…
4023.explicacion: Teresa Perales and Daniel Molina are athletes with disabilities who have won medals at the Paralympic Games. So they are «campeones paraolímpicos», not musicians or actors. Teresa Perales is a swimmer and one of Spain's most decorated athletes.

4024.texto: What do Spaniards eat on the night of 31 December to celebrate the new year?
4024.explicacion: On the night of 31 December, «Nochevieja», Spaniards eat twelve grapes («uvas»), one with each chime of the clock at midnight. It is a way to welcome the new year and wish for good luck. Tip: twelve grapes for the twelve months.

4025.explicacion: «Maruja Mallo» was a painter of the Generation of '27, and she painted «La verbena» in 1927. Carmen Maura and Clara Lago are film actresses, not painters. Tip: Maruja Mallo is the only painter in the list.

4026.texto: In which Spanish museum can you see Picasso's Guernica?
4026.explicacion: Picasso's «Guernica» hangs in the «Museo Reina Sofía» in Madrid, the museum of modern and contemporary art. The Prado mainly shows older art, such as Velázquez and Goya. Tip: Reina Sofía, 20th-century art, Guernica.

4027.texto: Which Spanish woman writer writes in another official language of Spain?
4027.explicacion: «Mercè Rodoreda» wrote in Catalan («catalán»), an official language in Catalonia together with Spanish. Her best-known novel is «La plaza del Diamante». Almudena Grandes and Ana María Matute wrote in Spanish. Tip: the name Mercè is spelled the Catalan way.

4028.texto: Which three cultures lived together in medieval Spain?
4028.explicacion: In medieval Spain three cultures lived side by side: «la cristiana, la judía y la musulmana» (Christian, Jewish and Muslim). Cities such as Toledo and Córdoba are examples. The Phoenicians and Greeks came much earlier, in ancient times. Tip: three religions, three cultures.

4029.explicacion: 6 December is «el Día de la Constitución» (Constitution Day), because on that day in 1978 Spaniards approved the Constitution in a referendum. It is a national holiday. Columbus's arrival is celebrated on 12 October and Book Day on 23 April.

4030.texto: Which city was a centre of science in Al-Andalus, where medicine and astronomy were studied?
4030.explicacion: In Al-Andalus, «Córdoba» was a great city with schools and libraries where people studied medicine, astronomy and mathematics. Scholars such as Averroes and Maimonides lived there. Madrid and Barcelona were not centres of Al-Andalus. Tip: Córdoba, city of the Mosque and of scholars.

4031.texto: In which Spanish city is the Guggenheim Museum?
4031.explicacion: The Guggenheim Museum is in «Bilbao», in the Basque Country, beside the estuary. It opened in 1997 and its titanium building is world-famous. Madrid has the Prado, and Valencia has the City of Arts and Sciences.

4032.texto: The Cervantes Prize is given to…
4032.explicacion: The «Premio Cervantes» is the most important prize for writers («escritores») in the Spanish language. It is named after Miguel de Cervantes, author of Don Quixote. It is not for actors or painters. Tip: Cervantes was a writer, so the prize is for writers.

4033.texto: Which award recognises the best actors and films?
