4033.explicacion: The «Premios Goya» are the Spanish film awards. Every year they honour the best actors, directors and films. The Nobel and the Cervantes mainly reward writers. Tip: the Goyas are Spain's big night of cinema.

4034.texto: Which awards promote scientific, cultural and humanistic values in Spain?
opciones: The Princess of Asturias Awards (Premios Princesa de Asturias).
4034.explicacion: The «Premios Princesa de Asturias» are presented every year in Oviedo. They honour people and institutions in science, culture, sport, communication and other fields. The Goyas are for cinema and the Cervantes is for writers. Tip: Princesa de Asturias means awards in many fields.

4035.texto: Which of these sports is very popular in Spain?
4035.explicacion: «El fútbol» (football) is the most popular sport in Spain: many people play it and watch it every week. Spain's men's team won the World Cup in 2010 and the women's team in 2023. Skiing and golf are played too, but they are less popular.

4036.texto: Which of these athletes plays tennis?
4036.explicacion: «Carlos Alcaraz» is a Spanish tennis player who has won several Grand Slam titles and has been world number one. Pau Gasol played basketball and Carlos Sainz drives racing cars. Tip: Alcaraz, racket; Gasol, basket; Sainz, steering wheel.

5001.texto: Which document must foreigners apply for to live legally in Spain?
opciones: The Documento Nacional de Identidad (DNI, national identity card).
The Tarjeta de Identidad de Extranjero (TIE, foreigner identity card).
The certificado de empadronamiento (local register certificate).
5001.explicacion: Foreigners living legally in Spain hold the «Tarjeta de Identidad de Extranjero (TIE)», which shows their NIE number and photo. The «DNI» is only for Spanish citizens, and the «empadronamiento» only shows where you live. Tip: the E in TIE stands for «Extranjero» (foreigner).
5001.nota: For the exam the answer is the TIE, but EU citizens do not need it: they register in the Central Register of Foreigners and get a registration certificate.

5002.texto: Which document certifies where the holder lives?
opciones: The certificado de empadronamiento (local register certificate).
5002.explicacion: The «certificado de empadronamiento» shows which municipality and address you live at. The town hall («ayuntamiento») issues it, and you need it for many procedures, such as healthcare or school. A birth certificate or driving licence does not show your address. Tip: «padrón», town hall, address.

5003.texto: What does the individual electronic record replace?
5003.explicacion: The «registro electrónico individual» replaces the «libro de familia» (family book). Now each person has their own digital record in the Civil Registry, with details of birth, marriage or children. The DNI and the driving licence still exist. Tip: the paper book becomes a digital record.

5004.texto: What is the minimum age to drive a car in Spain?
5004.explicacion: In Spain you must be «18 años» (18 years old) to get a B licence, which is the licence to drive a car. At 16 you can only ride some small motorbikes, with a different type of licence. Tip: adult age, 18, car.

5005.texto: You get your driving licence at…
opciones: the Dirección General de Tráfico (DGT, Directorate-General for Traffic).
5005.explicacion: The «Dirección General de Tráfico (DGT)» runs the driving tests and issues driving licences. It also handles traffic rules and vehicles. The National Police issue the DNI, and the Civil Registry records births and marriages. Tip: Tráfico means licences and cars.

5006.texto: To get a driving licence you must pass…
opciones: a theory test and a practical test.
5006.explicacion: To get a driving licence you need to pass two tests: «un examen teórico y otro práctico». First a theory test on traffic rules, then a practical test driving on the road. One test alone is not enough. Tip: theory plus practice, both.

5007.texto: Where do you apply for the libro de familia (family book)?
5007.explicacion: The «libro de familia» is handled by the «Registro Civil» (Civil Registry), where births, marriages and deaths are recorded. Social Security deals with healthcare and pensions, and the police issue the DNI. Tip: family, births and weddings mean Registro Civil.
5007.nota: For the exam the answer is the Registro Civil, but the paper family book is now being replaced by the individual electronic record, which the Registro Civil also keeps.

5008.texto: Which of these TV channels is regional (autonómico)?
5008.explicacion: «Canal Sur» is the public television of Andalusia, an autonomous community, so it is an «autonómico» (regional) channel. Telecinco and Nova broadcast to all of Spain. Other regional channels include TV3 in Catalonia and Telemadrid. Tip: «Sur» means south, like Andalusia.

5009.texto: How long is maternity or paternity leave?
5009.explicacion: Today, birth and childcare leave lasts «19 semanas» (19 weeks) for each parent, the mother and the other parent. It is the same for both and cannot be transferred to the other parent. The figures of 12 and 22 weeks are wrong. Tip: 19 weeks, for mum and for dad.

5010.texto: What is the maximum blood alcohol level allowed for drivers, in grams per litre (g/l)?
5010.explicacion: In Spain, the general blood alcohol limit for driving is 0.5 grams per litre. For new drivers and professional drivers the limit is lower: 0.3 g/l. Tip: remember «half a gram», which is 0.5 (written «0,5» in Spanish).
5010.nota: For the exam the answer is 0.5 g/l, the general limit, although new and professional drivers have a lower limit of 0.3 g/l.

5011.texto: What is the most common type of home in Spain?
5011.explicacion: Most people in Spain live in flats, that is, homes inside a building shared with neighbours. Country houses and detached houses are less common, especially in cities. Tip: a flat is a «piso», and that is why Spaniards talk so much about the «comunidad de vecinos» (residents' association).

5012.texto: Which autonomous community is known for the quality of its olive oil?
5012.explicacion: «Andalucía» (Andalusia) is the largest olive oil producer in Spain and in the world; the province of Jaén alone has millions of olive trees. Cantabria is known for dairy products and La Rioja for its wine. Tip: think of the olive groves of the south.

5013.texto: What is the name of the inspection that cars must compulsorily pass?
5013.explicacion: The «ITV» (Inspección Técnica de Vehículos) is the compulsory roadworthiness test that checks a car is safe and does not pollute too much. The IBI is a tax on homes and land, and the ITE is an inspection of buildings. Tip: the «V» in ITV stands for «vehículos».

5014.texto: The snack that comes with a drink in bars and restaurants is called…
5014.explicacion: A «tapa» is a small portion of food served with your drink in many bars, sometimes for free. A «bocadillo» is a filled bread roll and the «primer plato» is the first course of a set menu. Tip: going out with friends for drinks and snacks is called going «de tapas».

5015.texto: Where do you apply for the health card (tarjeta sanitaria)?
5015.explicacion: You apply for the health card at the «centro de salud» (health centre) for your address, usually with your «empadronamiento» (local registration) certificate. The police do not issue it, and the Ministry of Health does not deal with individual applications. Tip: the card is for seeing a doctor, so you get it where your doctor is.

5016.texto: How many children does a family need to be a large family?
5016.explicacion: As a general rule, a family is a «familia numerosa» (large family) when it has three or more children. This official status gives access to help and discounts, for example on public transport or university fees. Tip: «numerosa» starts at 3 children.
5016.nota: For the exam the answer is «3 children», although the law also recognises some families with 2 children in special cases, for example when there is a disability.

opciones: only between people of the same sex.
between people of the same and of different sex.
only between people of different sex.
5017.explicacion: Since 2005, in Spain people of different sex and people of the same sex can marry, with the same rights. So the correct answer is «entre personas del mismo y diferente sexo». Tip: the options with «solo» (only) are wrong, because the law allows both.

5018.texto: Dog owners must register their dogs with…
5018.explicacion: Dogs must be listed in the animal register of the «Ayuntamiento» (town council) where they live, and they must also have a microchip. The police and the Ministry of Justice do not keep this register. Tip: the town council keeps the «padrón» of residents and also the register of pets.

5019.texto: The main ingredients of Spanish omelette are eggs and…
5019.explicacion: Spanish omelette, also called «tortilla de patatas», is made with eggs and «patatas» (potatoes), and many people add onion. Peppers and tomatoes are not a main ingredient. Tip: its other name, «tortilla de patatas» (potato omelette), already gives you the answer.

5020.texto: Which is one of the best-known Spanish dishes internationally?
5020.explicacion: «Gazpacho» is a cold soup made with tomato, pepper, cucumber, garlic and olive oil. It comes from Andalusia and is famous all over the world. Pizza and pasta are Italian dishes. Tip: choose the only Spanish word in the list.

5021.texto: Which of these television channels is public?
5021.explicacion: «La 1» is a channel of RTVE, Spain's state-owned public radio and television. Tele 5 and Antena 3 are private channels owned by companies. Tip: «La 1» and «La 2» are the traditional public channels of RTVE.

5022.texto: In a residents' association (comunidad de vecinos), one of the rules is…
opciones: to open the door to the postman.
not to disturb others with noise.
5022.explicacion: In a «comunidad de vecinos» you must respect other people's rest and «no molestar con ruido» (not disturb with noise), especially at night. Cleaning the shared areas is usually done by someone who is paid for it, and opening the door to the postman is not a rule. Tip: think of respect for your neighbours.

5023.texto: Which of these is the main ingredient of Valencian paella?
5023.explicacion: Valencian paella is a dish of «arroz» (rice) cooked in a large, flat pan, which is also called a «paella». The traditional recipe has chicken, rabbit and vegetables, but no chorizo or chickpeas. Tip: no rice, no paella.

5024.texto: Cider (sidra) is a typical drink of…
5024.explicacion: «Sidra» (cider) is a drink made from apples and is typical of «Asturias», in the north of Spain. There it is poured in a special way, from high above with the bottle raised. Valencia is famous for paella and the Canary Islands for bananas.

5025.texto: Spaniards have two surnames; the first one is…
opciones: can be either the mother's or the father's.
5025.explicacion: Spaniards have two «apellidos» (surnames): one from the father and one from the mother. Since 2017 parents choose the order, so the first «puede ser el de la madre o el del padre». That is why the options with «obligatoriamente» (compulsorily) are wrong.

5026.explicacion: Spain's National Day is the «12 de octubre» (12 October), the day Columbus reached America in 1492. 6 December is Constitution Day and 15 August is the religious holiday of the Assumption. Tip: link 12 October with 1492.

5027.texto: On which days do most shops or small businesses usually close?
5027.explicacion: Most small shops close on «domingos» (Sundays), the weekly day of rest. On Mondays and Saturday afternoons many of them are open. In tourist areas and some shopping centres, shops may also open on Sundays. In the exam, look for «Los domingos».

5028.texto: Where do you get a passport?
5028.explicacion: Passports and the DNI (identity card) are issued at a «comisaría de policía», in National Police offices, usually by appointment. The «registro civil» records births and marriages, and the town council manages the «padrón» (residents' register). Tip: identity documents mean the police station.

5029.texto: The Ministry of Equality is responsible for fighting gender-based violence and…
5029.explicacion: The «Ministerio de Igualdad» (Ministry of Equality) works against gender-based violence and against «discriminación» (discrimination), for example because of sex or sexual orientation. Equality means everyone has the same rights. Tip: the opposite of equality is discrimination, and you do not fight solidarity.

5030.texto: Which autonomous community is known for the quality of its cavas?
5030.explicacion: «Cava» is a sparkling wine, and most of it is produced in «Cataluña» (Catalonia), especially in the Penedès area. Galicia is famous for its white wines and Castile-La Mancha for Manchego cheese. Tip: «cava» and «Cataluña» both start with «ca».

5031.texto: Which document do you need to receive medical care in the public health system?
5031.explicacion: To see a doctor in the public health system you need the «tarjeta sanitaria» (health card), issued by your autonomous community. A passport is for travelling and a birth certificate proves your personal details, but neither gives access to a doctor. Tip: «sanitaria» comes from «sanidad» (health care).

5032.texto: Compared with the Peninsula, the time in the Canary Islands is…
5032.explicacion: The Canary Islands are «una hora menos» (one hour behind) the Peninsula: when it is 12 in Madrid, it is 11 in the Canaries. That is why Spanish radio often says «una hora menos en Canarias». Tip: that radio phrase is exactly the answer.

5033.texto: To get into university you must pass an assessment test called…
opciones: University Entrance Exam (Prueba de Acceso a la Universidad).
5033.explicacion: The official name of the university entrance exam is «Prueba de Acceso a la Universidad» (PAU). Many people call it «Selectividad», but that is a popular name, not the official one. Tip: the official name says what it is for: access to university.
5033.nota: For the exam the answer is «Prueba de Acceso a la Universidad», although people commonly say «Selectividad» and some regions use other acronyms such as EBAU or EvAU.

5034.texto: Which of these products does Spain need to import from other countries?
5034.explicacion: Spain has almost no «petróleo» (crude oil) of its own, so it buys it from other countries for energy and transport. On the other hand, it is the world's largest olive oil producer and makes many medicines. Tip: petroleum comes from abroad; olive oil comes from Spanish olive trees.

5035.texto: What kind of taxes do citizens have to pay in Spain?
opciones: Direct taxes such as IRPF (personal income tax).
5035.explicacion: People in Spain pay both kinds: «impuestos directos e indirectos». IRPF is a direct tax because it depends on how much you earn. IVA (VAT) is indirect because you pay it when you buy something. The other two options name only one type, so they are incomplete.

5036.texto: Adults without the Bachillerato (upper secondary school certificate) can study at University by taking a special test from the age of…
5036.explicacion: From «25 años», adults can enter University without the «Bachillerato» by passing a special entrance test for older students. At 18, the usual path is to finish the «Bachillerato» and take the ordinary exam. Tip: remember «over 25» as the special route.

5037.texto: Where might you find the following rule: “Do not step on the grass or pick the flowers”?
5037.explicacion: The sign «No pisar el césped, ni arrancar flores» is typical of parks and public gardens, which are «zonas de recreo» (recreation areas). A theatre has no grass or flowers. A football stadium has grass, but no flowers to pick.

5038.texto: The Bachillerato (upper secondary education) in Spain…
opciones: is the education for pupils aged 14 to 16.
5038.explicacion: The «Bachillerato» is made up of «dos cursos académicos», usually from age 16 to 18. It is not compulsory: compulsory schooling ends with the «ESO», which covers ages 12 to 16. Tip: two years after the ESO.

5039.texto: Value Added Tax (IVA) is one of the…
5039.explicacion: «IVA» (VAT) belongs to the «impuestos indirectos»: it does not depend on what you earn but on what you buy. It is included in the price of goods and services. Income tax (IRPF) and corporate tax are direct taxes.

5040.texto: What number do workers receive when they start their first job?
5040.explicacion: When you start your first job, you get a «número de la Seguridad Social» (Social Security number). It stays with you for your whole working life and is used for healthcare, pensions and unemployment benefits. Your passport number has nothing to do with employment.

opciones: can decide how many places they offer.
can hire any teachers they want.
5041.explicacion: State schools «son gratuitos» because they are paid for with taxes. They cannot freely choose their teachers or number of places: teachers pass public exams («oposiciones») and the education authorities set the places. Tip: public means free.

5042.texto: Which of these ports is one of the main ports in Spain?
5042.explicacion: «Algeciras», in the province of Cádiz, is one of the busiest ports in Spain and in Europe. It lies next to the Strait of Gibraltar, where a huge number of ships pass. Tenerife and Alicante also have ports, but they are less important.

5043.texto: A colegio concertado (state-funded private school) is a private school that…
opciones: receives money from the public authorities.
is funded by the pupils' parents.
5043.explicacion: A «colegio concertado» is privately run but «recibe dinero de la Administración» through an agreement (a «concierto») with the State. That is why basic schooling there is free or almost free. If only the parents paid, it would be an ordinary private school.

5044.texto: Spain mainly exports products to countries…
5044.explicacion: Most Spanish exports go to «la Unión Europea», especially France, Germany, Italy and Portugal. They are close neighbours in a single market with no customs between them. Latin America and North Africa buy far less.

5045.explicacion: Public libraries are free «para todos»: children, adults, unemployed people and workers alike. To borrow books you only need a library card («carné de la biblioteca»), which is also free. Tip: public means open to everyone.

5046.texto: Which of these products does Spain export more than it imports?
5046.explicacion: According to the official manual, footwear («Calzado») is a product Spain exports more than it imports, thanks to a strong shoe industry in places such as Alicante and La Rioja. Gas, by contrast, is almost entirely imported because Spain produces very little.
5046.nota: For the exam, the manual's answer «Calzado» counts, although in recent years Spain's footwear imports have been similar to or even higher than its exports.

5047.texto: A person over 18 can obtain the Graduado en Educación Secundaria Obligatoria (compulsory secondary education certificate) at…
5047.explicacion: Adults over 18 can earn the «ESO» certificate at a «Centro de Educación de Personas Adultas» (adult education centre), whose timetables suit people who work. Primary schools are for children, and university comes after the «Bachillerato».

opciones: can be intermediate or higher level.
5048.explicacion: Vocational training («FP») teaches a trade and can be «de grado medio o superior» (intermediate or higher level). Intermediate courses follow the «ESO», and higher courses follow the «Bachillerato». It is not compulsory and not only for people over 25.

5049.texto: Where do we go to see the family doctor or the paediatrician?
5049.explicacion: To see your «médico de familia» (GP) or paediatrician, you go to your local «centro de salud», where primary care is provided. Hospitals are for serious emergencies or specialists, and pharmacies sell medicines but do not offer consultations.

5050.texto: For how many years is the European Health Insurance Card valid?
5050.explicacion: The «tarjeta sanitaria europea» (European Health Insurance Card) is normally valid for «dos años». It lets you receive necessary medical care in other European Union countries and is requested free of charge from the «Seguridad Social». Tip: check the expiry date before travelling.

5051.texto: At what time do people usually have dinner in Spain?
5051.explicacion: Spaniards usually have dinner late, «a las 21 o 22 h» (9 or 10 p.m.). Mealtimes are later than in many countries: lunch is often around 2 or 3 p.m. At 6 p.m. people may have a snack called «merienda», not dinner.

5052.texto: What is the single telephone number for any emergency?
5052.explicacion: «112» is the single number for any emergency in Spain and across the European Union: police, fire brigade or ambulance. It is free and works 24 hours a day. 911 is the emergency number in the United States, not in Spain.

5053.texto: Which of these newspapers is published nationwide?
5053.explicacion: «El País» is a national newspaper, sold and read all over Spain. «El Diario Vasco» and «La Voz de Galicia» are regional papers that mainly cover the Basque Country and Galicia. Tip: a region's name in the title points to a regional paper.

5054.texto: Where are stamps and tobacco sold?
5054.explicacion: Stamps and tobacco are sold at the «estanco», which you can spot by its brown sign reading «Tabacos». A «quiosco» (kiosk) sells newspapers and magazines, and a pharmacy sells medicines. Tip: estanco means tobacco and stamps.

5055.texto: When can you call the helpline for victims of gender-based violence?
5055.explicacion: The «016» helpline for victims of gender-based violence works «las 24 horas del día», every day of the year. Calls are free, help is available in many languages, and the call does not show on the phone bill. That way any victim can ask for help at any time.

5056.texto: The organisation that works for the integration of people with visual impairments is…
opciones: the ONCE (National Organisation of Spanish Blind People).
5056.explicacion: «la ONCE» is the National Organisation of Spanish Blind People. It works for the inclusion of blind and partially sighted people and is well known for its lottery ticket, the «cupón». Unicef helps children, and Cáritas helps people in poverty.

5057.texto: The Camino de Santiago (Way of St James) is…
5057.explicacion: The Way of St James is listed by UNESCO as «Patrimonio de la Humanidad» (World Heritage). It is a historic pilgrimage route ending in Santiago de Compostela. It is not a railway: people travel it on foot, by bike or on horseback.
5057.nota: For the exam, the answer is «Patrimonio de la Humanidad», although many hikers do walk the Camino, so the third option is not entirely false.

5058.texto: Which state television channel broadcasts national and international news non-stop?
5058.explicacion: «Canal 24 horas» is the public RTVE channel that broadcasts national and international news all day, non-stop. The name says it all: 24 hours of news. «Teledeporte» shows sport, and «La 1» is a general-interest channel.

5059.texto: The free helpline for victims of gender-based violence is…
5059.explicacion: «016» is the free helpline for victims of gender-based violence. It is open 24 hours and leaves no trace on the phone bill. «091» is the number for the «Policía Nacional» (National Police), and «112» is for any emergency.

5060.texto: In Spain, the train network can be long-distance, medium-distance and…
5060.explicacion: Spain has long-distance trains, medium-distance trains and commuter trains, called «cercanías». Commuter trains connect a big city with the nearby towns and suburbs, and many people use them to get to work. Tip: «cercanías» comes from «cerca», which means «near».

5061.texto: What is forbidden at the entrance of a school?
5061.explicacion: Smoking is banned in schools and at their entrances to protect children's health. Driving a car or selling drinks in the street is not forbidden there. Remember: «Fumar un cigarrillo» (smoking a cigarette) is not allowed where children study.

5062.texto: Which qualification do you get after finishing an intermediate-level Vocational Training (Formación Profesional) course?
opciones: Graduado en ESO (compulsory secondary education certificate).
5062.explicacion: After finishing an intermediate-level Vocational Training course, students get the «Técnico» (Technician) qualification. The higher level gives «Técnico Superior» (Higher Technician). «Bachiller» and «Graduado en ESO» belong to other types of study. Tip: intermediate FP = «Técnico».

5063.texto: Which title do you get after completing a doctoral thesis in Spain?
5063.explicacion: The doctoral thesis is the final piece of work in university studies. A person who presents and passes it gets the title of «Doctor». Before that, students do the «Grado» (bachelor's degree) and then the «Máster». Easy order to remember: «Grado», «Máster», «Doctor».

5064.texto: Where do you buy prescription medicines?
5064.explicacion: Prescription medicines are bought at the pharmacy, the «farmacia». The doctor at the health centre or hospital writes the prescription, the «receta», but does not sell medicines. Remember: the doctor prescribes, the pharmacy sells. Pharmacies have a green cross.

5065.texto: Which of these three recommendations can we find in a park?
opciones: Please pay for your ticket with the exact amount.
5065.explicacion: In parks you often see signs saying «No pisar el césped» (keep off the grass), to protect the grass and plants. The other two rules, paying for the ticket with the exact amount and the luggage rules, belong to public transport, such as buses or trains.

5066.texto: Which of the following is compulsory for a car owner in Spain?
5066.explicacion: In Spain, every car on the road must have compulsory insurance, the «seguro». Insurance pays for the damage the car may cause to other people in an accident. A garage and an alarm are useful, but they are not compulsory.

5067.explicacion: «Adolfo Suárez Madrid-Barajas» Airport is in Madrid and it is the largest airport in Spain. It is named after the first Prime Minister of Spain's democracy. Barcelona's airport is called «Josep Tarradellas El Prat».

5068.texto: In a car, wearing a seat belt is compulsory…
5068.explicacion: In Spain, the seat belt, the «cinturón de seguridad», is compulsory in all seats, «en todos los asientos», both front and back. It is not only for the driver or the front seats. Young children must also travel in a special car seat suited to their size.

5069.texto: What is the speed limit on the motorway?
5069.explicacion: On Spanish motorways, «autopistas» and «autovías», the general speed limit for cars is 120 km/h. Driving at 150 km/h is not allowed, and 90 km/h is the limit on many ordinary roads. Tip: «autopista» = 120.

5070.texto: Giving up your seat to people with reduced mobility is a rule we find displayed in…
5070.explicacion: On buses, the metro and trains there are priority seats and signs asking you to give your seat to older people, pregnant women or people with reduced mobility. This rule is typical of public transport, the «transporte público», because many people travel standing up.

5071.texto: Which means of public transport has a green light on when it is free?
5071.explicacion: In Spain, taxis have a green light on the roof. When the green light is on, the taxi is free, «libre», and you can stop it by raising your hand. Buses and trams have fixed stops and do not use this light.

5072.texto: What must you do if you have a dog?
5072.explicacion: If you have a dog, you must have it fitted with a «microchip» and vaccinated, for example against rabies. The microchip identifies the dog and its owner. You must also keep it on a lead in the street and always pick up its droppings.

5073.texto: Spaniards need a passport to travel to…
5073.explicacion: China, «China», is not in the European Union, so Spaniards need a passport, the «pasaporte», to travel there. To go to Italy or Germany, which are EU countries, the national identity card, the «DNI», is enough. Tip: outside Europe, take your passport.

5074.texto: What is the minimum working age in Spain?
5074.explicacion: In Spain, the minimum working age is 16, «16 años». Between 16 and 18, young people need permission from their parents or guardians, and they cannot work at night or do overtime. From 18, there are no special limits.

5075.texto: Which sector carries the most weight in the Spanish economy?
5075.explicacion: The services sector, «Servicios», is the most important part of the Spanish economy: it employs most people and includes tourism, trade, healthcare and education. Agriculture and construction carry much less weight.

5076.texto: Spain is innovative in the sector of…
5076.explicacion: Spain is an innovative country in renewable energy, «energías renovables», especially wind and solar power. It has plenty of sun and wind, and Spanish companies work in many countries. Tip: sun and wind = «energías renovables».

5077.texto: What is the name of the most important employment law in Spain?
opciones: The Workers' Statute (El Estatuto de los Trabajadores).
The State Public Employment Service (El Servicio Público de Empleo Estatal).
5077.explicacion: The most important employment law is the «Estatuto de los Trabajadores» (Workers' Statute). It sets out the rights and duties of workers and employers: contracts, pay, holidays and dismissals. The «Constitución» is the country's general law, and the «SEPE» is an employment service, not a law.

5078.texto: Which of these shops is open 24 hours if necessary?
5078.explicacion: The pharmacy, the «Farmacia», can open 24 hours because of duty pharmacies, «farmacias de guardia»: every night and on public holidays, some pharmacies take turns to stay open. So you can always buy urgent medicines. Each pharmacy door shows which one is on duty.

5079.texto: Early childhood education (la educación infantil) in Spain…
5079.explicacion: Early childhood education, «educación infantil», in Spain has two cycles, «dos ciclos»: the first from 0 to 3 years old and the second from 3 to 6. It is not compulsory and it starts from birth, not at age 4. Compulsory education begins at 6.

5080.texto: When does the school calendar start?
5080.explicacion: In Spain, the school year starts in September, «septiembre», and ends in June. The exact dates vary a little between autonomous communities, «comunidades autónomas», but school always starts in September. In August, schools are closed for the summer holidays.

5081.texto: The Official Language Schools (Escuelas Oficiales de Idiomas)…
opciones: depend on the Cervantes Institute (Instituto Cervantes).
5081.explicacion: The «Escuelas Oficiales de Idiomas» are public centres where you can learn languages at low prices. In general they are for people over 16, «mayores de 16 años». They are not private and do not depend on the «Instituto Cervantes», but on the autonomous communities.
5081.nota: For the exam, the correct answer is «son para mayores de 16 años», but young people can also enrol from age 14 to study a language different from the one they study in ESO.

5082.texto: Which document shows the years of contributions to Social Security (Seguridad Social)?
opciones: Employment history report (Informe de vida laboral).
5082.explicacion: The «Informe de vida laboral» shows all your jobs and the days you have paid contributions to the «Seguridad Social». You can request it online for free. The «finiquito» is the final payment when a contract ends, and the «certificado de profesionalidad» proves a training qualification.

5083.texto: A company's collective agreements are those signed with the workers' representatives about…
5083.explicacion: A collective agreement, «convenio colectivo», is an agreement between the company and the workers' representatives about working conditions, «condiciones laborales»: pay, working hours, holidays and other rights. It is not about the company's future or its customers. Tip: «convenio» = working conditions.

5084.texto: In which of these sectors does Spain stand out?
5084.explicacion: Spain stands out in tourism, «turismo»: it is one of the most visited countries in the world, with more than 80 million tourists a year. They come for the sun, the beaches, the culture and the food. Tourism is a very important part of its economy.
5084.nota: For the exam, the correct answer is «En el turismo», although Spain is also one of Europe's largest car manufacturers.
